passages.scripture: We must pay closer attention, therefore, to what we have heard, so that we do not drift away.

lines.text: We have heard God's message, spoken through His Son, Jesus.
Therefore we must pay closer attention to God's message.
So we do not drift away from God's message.

passages.scripture: For if the message spoken by angels was binding, and every transgression and disobedience received its just punishment, how shall we escape if we neglect such a great salvation? This salvation was first announced by the Lord, was confirmed to us by those who heard Him, and was affirmed by God through signs, wonders, various miracles, and gifts of the Holy Spirit distributed according to His will.

lines.text: Long ago, God's message came to people through angels.
This message was binding — it had to be obeyed.
Every transgression and disobedience received a just punishment.
The Lord Jesus was the first to proclaim a great salvation.
Eyewitnesses like the apostles heard Jesus proclaim this great salvation.
These eyewitnesses confirmed this salvation to us — they assured us it is true.
God Himself also affirmed this salvation with signs, wonders, and various miracles.
God also affirmed this salvation through gifts of the Holy Spirit.
God distributed these gifts according to His will.
So if we neglect this great salvation, how can we escape?

passages.scripture: For it is not to angels that He has subjected the world to come, about which we are speaking.

lines.text: We are speaking about the world to come — not this present world, but the new heavens and new earth God will create.
God did not put this coming world under the authority of angels.

passages.scripture: But somewhere it is testified in these words: “What is man that You are mindful of him, or the son of man that You care for him?

lines.text: Somewhere in the Scriptures, someone testified to God about man.
This person asked God, 'What is man, that You are mindful of him?'
This person also asked God, 'What is the son of man, that You care for him?'

passages.scripture: You made him a little lower than the angels; You crowned him with glory and honor and placed everything under his feet.” When God subjected all things to him, He left nothing outside of his control. Yet at present we do not see everything subject to him.

lines.text: God, You made man a little lower than the angels.
God, You crowned man with glory and honor.
God, You placed everything under man's feet.
God subjected all things to man.
God left nothing outside of man's control.
But right now, we do not yet see everything under man's control.

passages.scripture: But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, now crowned with glory and honor because He suffered death, so that by the grace of God He might taste death for everyone.

lines.text: But we see Jesus.
God made Jesus a little lower than the angels.
Now God has crowned Jesus with glory and honor.
God crowned Jesus because He suffered death.
By God's grace, Jesus tasted death for everyone.

passages.scripture: In bringing many sons to glory, it was fitting for God, for whom and through whom all things exist, to make the author of their salvation perfect through suffering.

lines.text: All things exist for God.
All things also exist through God.
God is bringing many sons and daughters to glory.
Through suffering, God completely prepared Jesus to save the children of God.
This was fitting for God.

passages.scripture: For both the One who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are of the same family. So Jesus is not ashamed to call them brothers.

lines.text: Jesus is the One who makes people holy.
Believers are the ones Jesus makes holy.
Jesus and these believers belong to the same family.
So Jesus is not ashamed to call these believers His brothers and sisters.

passages.scripture: He says: “I will proclaim Your name to My brothers; I will sing Your praises in the assembly.”

lines.text: Jesus says to God, 'I will proclaim Your name to My brothers and sisters.'
Jesus also says to God, 'I will sing Your praises in the assembly of God's people.'

passages.scripture: And again: “I will put My trust in Him.” And once again: “Here am I, and the children God has given Me.”

lines.text: Again Jesus says, 'I will put My trust in God.'
And again Jesus says, 'Here I am, and the children God has given Me.'

passages.scripture: Now since the children have flesh and blood, He too shared in their humanity, so that by His death He might destroy him who holds the power of death, that is, the devil, and free those who all their lives were held in slavery by their fear of death.

lines.text: God's children are human, with flesh and blood.
So Jesus also shared this same human flesh and blood.
Jesus became human so that He could die.
The one who holds the power of death is the devil.
And all their lives, people were enslaved by their fear of death.
Jesus defeated the devil.
So Jesus set these people free.

passages.scripture: For surely it is not the angels He helps, but the descendants of Abraham.

lines.text: It is surely not the angels that Jesus helps.
But Jesus helps the descendants of Abraham — those who share Abraham's faith.

passages.scripture: For this reason He had to be made like His brothers in every way, so that He might become a merciful and faithful high priest in service to God, in order to make atonement for the sins of the people.

lines.text: So Jesus had to be made like His human brothers in every way — the eternal Son of God became human.
Because Jesus was fully human, He could become a merciful and faithful high priest for us.
As our high priest, Jesus serves God.
So Jesus offered a priestly sacrifice to make atonement for the sins of the people — He paid for our sins.

passages.scripture: Because He Himself suffered when He was tempted, He is able to help those who are being tempted.

lines.text: Jesus Himself suffered when He was tempted.
So Jesus is able to help those who are being tempted.
